item.text: {"question_id":"3B.3","answer":"The 2023 record is mixed and does not establish direct presidential incitement against protected domestic groups. Tshisekedi publicly promoted love, unity, equality, and opposition to divisiveness, and stated that Congolese law prohibited and severely sanctioned tribal, ethnic, racial, and xenophobic hate speech (BATCH-0020-E015; BATCH-0016-E003). However, he also threatened to target without hesitation or regret people he considered threats to national security, warned that foreigners would manufacture candidates, and used strongly hostile language toward Rwanda and M23; the latter concerned an armed external conflict and is not by itself domestic incitement against a protected civilian group (BATCH-0003-E010; BATCH-0018-E007; BATCH-0007-E013). During the campaign, a UDPS provincial governor made a statement that the media regulator deemed incitement to ethnic-regional hatred, exclusion, and discrimination; UDPS supporters were also recorded attacking opposition actors, while ACLED found ruling-party supporters both highly targeted and the most active group in violence against other political parties. These facts establish a harmful aligned-party environment, but the supplied evidence does not show that Tshisekedi authored or endorsed the governor’s statement, ordered the attacks, or took or failed to take a documented disciplinary measure after notice (BATCH-0002-E017; BATCH-0006-E004; BATCH-0010-E021). The evidence therefore supports adverse concern about presidential rhetoric and insufficiently demonstrated control or remedy, but not a finding of proven personal incitement or causally demonstrated responsibility for subsequent
